newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Daewoo Elec SA warns of half year loss.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo Elec SA warns of half year loss.

text.p: South Africa's Daewoo Electronics SA Ltd said on Tuesday that it will report a significant loss for the half year to June 30 due to tougher-than-expected market conditions.

The firm warned in its annual chairman's statement that the year ahead would be difficult to forecast and unlikely to improve much before the second half of the year, but Daewoo said things had taken a turn for the worse.
"Market conditions in the consumer electronics industry have proved to be weaker than anticipated," the firm said.
It blamed high interest rates, delayed purchases of large household electrical goods and a flood of illegal imports.
"Shareholders are advised that, in respect of the interim results, a significant loss will be attributable to shareholders," the firm said.
Daewoo had expected some of its losses in the period to be offset by a refund of duty paid since November, 1995, on imported satellite receivers.
Daewoo had believed the receivers had been imported under an incorrect customs rating and applied for a refund of 13.3 million rand. However, customs turned down the request.
Daewoo said it is currently taking legal advice on pursuing the claim further.

The group said it could not yet comment on prospects for the full year and warned the legal fight with customs could knock satellite receiver sales in the second half as it would interfere with pricing and costing.
The firm warned its shareholders to exercise caution when dealing in its shares until its interim results are published later in August.
